content: Globals --- Other Generates a menu with the provided index as the currently selected item. Parameters - tableRows (Array) - tableHeadings (Array) - tableClass (string) Returns - Object. Builds the add-exercise form's DOM structure. No event wiring here - see exercisePicker.js's own note on why that has to happen after this is attached into the real document and rendered. Primary and secondary are two separate multi-selects (rather than one picker with a per-muscle rank) - a real exercise's muscles split cleanly into those two buckets, and a plain multi-select needs no dynamic add/remove row UI to support picking several of each. Parameters - muscles (Array) — musclePriority()'s shape (every real muscle, not just priority ones) - becomes both selects' options Returns - Object Wires the form's submit button - see addExerciseForm's own note on timing. Parameters - form (Object) - onSubmit (function) — ({ name, description, primaryMuscleIds, secondaryMuscleIds }) = void Generates a menu with the provided index as the currently selected item. Parameters - currentIndex (number) Returns - DomItem Builds the muscle - exercise picker's DOM structure. No event wiring here - fullAddEventListener needs a complete parentItem chain up to the real document root (it throws otherwise), which a freshly-built, not-yet-attached DomItem doesn't have yet. Call wireExercisePickerEvents once this is attached into the real document and rendered. Parameters - priorityRows (Array) — musclePriority()'s shape, ordered by priority - becomes the muscle dropdown's options, top priority first Returns - Object Wires the picker's change events, once it's attached into the real document and rendered - see exercisePicker's own note on why this can't happen at construction time. Parameters - picker (Object) - onMuscleChange (function) — (muscleId: string) = void - onExerciseChange (function) — (exerciseId: string) = void Parameters - session (Object null) — getLastSession()'s shape, or null if never logged Returns - DomItem Builds the log-workout form's DOM structure. No event wiring here - see exercisePicker.js's own note on why that has to happen after this is attached into the real document and rendered. Returns - Object Reads the form's current field values, independent of which button triggered it. Parameters - form (Object) Wires the form's submit and update buttons - see logWorkoutForm's own note on timing. Parameters - form (Object) - onSubmit (function) — ({ weightEffort, sets, reps, note, date }) = void, logs a brand new entry - onUpdate (function) — ({ weightEffort, sets, reps, note, date }) = void, corrects the most recently shown entry Generates a table ranking muscles by how much they need attention right now. Parameters - priorityRows (Array) — musclePriority()'s shape: \[{ muscleId, name, daysSinceLastWorked, timesWorkedThisWeek, needsPriority }] Returns - Object. Generates a table for a workout plan. Returns - DomItem Copy the real database/ directory into an isolated test directory, so insert/update tests have real seed data to work with without ever touching the actual database/ this app runs against. Parameters - destination Rank muscles by how much they need attention right now, from a real read of the database: every muscle (including ones never worked at all), and every workout row with its muscles already joined on (see workout()/musclePriority.test.js for the exact query shape this expects). A muscle needs priority once it's past its recovery window, or hasn't been worked often enough this week yet - whichever muscle has gone longest without being worked sorts first. Parameters - muscles — every row from read muscles - workoutsWithMuscles — every row from the workouts-joined-to-muscles query, each carrying a .muscles array (the muscles that workout's exercise worked) - today — injectable for testing; defaults to the real current time Rank every muscle by how much it needs attention right now, from a real read of the database. Parameters - today — injectable for testing; defaults to the real current time Every exercise linked to a given muscle, via exercise muscle. Parameters - muscleId The most recently logged workout for a given exercise, or null if it's never been logged. Parameters - exerciseId Log a new workout entry. Parameters - exerciseId - weightEffort - sets - reps - note - date — defaults to today, in the same 'YYYY-MM-DD' shape the rest of the data uses - order — where this entry falls among others logged the same day (defaults to first) Update an existing workout entry - e.g. correcting the plan with what was actually done. Parameters - workoutId - changes — any subset of weightEffort/sets/reps/note to change Add a new exercise, with the muscles it works (primary/secondary, by whatever rank you give). Parameters - name - description - muscleAssignments (Array.\ ) — one row per muscle this exercise works
